instructions:
You translate one page of Alexander Grothendieck's handwritten mathematical notes (Montpellier archive) from French
into English. The page is a LaTeX transcription of the manuscript. Some passages are already in English (Grothendieck
wrote parts of these notes in English); keep those exactly as they are.

Write the English version of the whole page, as a faithful raw translation for mathematicians: close to the
wording, keeping Grothendieck's telegraphic style, question marks and hesitations. Do not smooth, complete,
correct or explain anything. Three rules from our readers:
- "sans doute" means "probably" (not "without doubt");
- write abbreviations out in English (for example "rat/K" -> "rational over K");
- an inserted adjective (in \inserted{...}) may move to its natural English position, still inside its \inserted{...}.

Keep every piece of LaTeX exactly as it is:
- every macro and its arguments' structure: \scanpage{...}, \mspage{...}, \margin{...}, \deleted{...},
  \inserted{...}, \unsure{...}, \illegible{...}, \uline{...}, \diagram{...}, environments, line breaks of displays;
- every formula, symbol and diagram: change no mathematics at all, not even an obvious slip;
- \scanpage and \mspage lines unchanged, in their places.
Translate the French words inside \deleted, \inserted, \margin and \unsure too. An \unsure{a|b} with alternative
readings: translate each alternative and keep the | between them (if two French alternatives give the same English,
still keep both). French words inside \text{...} or \mathrm{...} in formulas: translate them only when they are
ordinary words (e.g. \text{si} -> \text{if}); keep names of objects and notation as they are.
Mathematical terms: use the standard English terms (champ -> stack, catégorie fibrée -> fibred category,
topos, site, faisceau -> sheaf, gerbe -> gerbe, fibration, cofibration, équivalence faible -> weak equivalence,
modèle fermé -> closed model, etc.).

Answer in exactly this form, with nothing before the first marker:
=====BEGIN TARGET_NEW=====
(the complete English page)
=====END TARGET_NEW=====
=====NOTES=====
(readings you were unsure how to translate, with the French; or "none")

Shelfmark 149, scan 127.

\scanpage{127}
\mspage{63}
\margin{Again the question arises whether $N_V=\operatorname{Norm}(I_V)$. One would like the germs of sections of $\mathcal E_L^{\bar L}$ over \deleted{$\mathcal E_K$} \inserted{$\mathcal E_{K_1}^{\bar K}$} to be associated \unsure{with the} points of the normalization $\unsure{\tilde{\mathfrak X}|\tilde{\mathcal Z}}_{L/K}$ of $\unsure{\mathfrak X|\mathcal Z}_{L/K}$ in $\bar L$ --- that they form a bundle over $\unsure{\tilde{\mathfrak X}|\tilde{\mathcal Z}}_{L/K}$, with fibres the $H^1(\deleted{\mathcal E_K}\inserted{\mathcal E_{K_1}}^{\unsure{G|\bar K}},I_V)\ldots$ This is associated with the formula (for such a \uline{section} \unsure{$s$} of $\mathcal E_L$ over $\mathcal E_K$) $\mathcal E_L^{(\mathcal E_K^0)}\simeq I_V$ --- linked to the conjecture that for $\forall$ open \unsure{subgroup} of $N_V^0$, or \unsure{simply} $\forall$ \unsure{subgroup} of $N_V$ whose image in $N_V/I_V$ is \unsure{open}, one has \deleted{\unsure{Centr|all}} $(\mathcal E_L^{\bar L})^{\unsure{\Gamma|\bar\Gamma}}=I_V$ (this for $\forall$ valuation ring $V$ of $L/K$, \unsure{presumed} to have residue field algebraic over $K$). In fact, the question is purely geometric !\ldots}
\unsure{under|under} this condition --- in fact the section comes from a section of the decomposition group $N_V$ over $\mathcal E_K$.

\noindent b) Let $U$ be an ``elementary'' model of $L$ over $K$, anabelian. Then every section of $\mathcal E_U^{\bar L}$ over $\mathcal E_K^{\bar K}$ lifts to a section of $\mathcal E_L^{\bar L}$ over $\mathcal E_K^{\bar K}$.

It can therefore be described in terms of a valuation ring $V$ of $L/K$, and when $V$ has a centre on $U$, \unsure{one need only} \unsure{concentrate} on the case of a point $x\in U$ rational over $K$, and of the section defined by $x$. In this case (still setting $\Gamma=\mathcal E_K^{\bar K}$) one again conjectures, of course
\[
(32)\qquad (\mathcal E_L^{\bar L})^{\Gamma^0}=(1)
\]
(and one can replace $\Gamma^0$ there by $\Gamma^0\unsure{\ne1)|\ne)|\subset}\deleted{\unsure{\Gamma}}$
--- but in fact this (by virtue of $\operatorname{Centr}_\Gamma(\Gamma^0)=(1)$) is equivalent to the analogous relation \deleted{$\pi_{L\unsure{/|,}K}^{\bar L}$}
\[
(33)\qquad (\pi_{L\unsure{/|,}K}^{\bar L})^{\Gamma^0}=(1)
\]
which \unsure{is} moreover deduced, by dévissage,
\margin{126}
=====END TARGET_NEW=====
=====NOTES=====
“Centr”: retained as mathematical notation, possibly for “centralisateur” (“centralizer”).
